display_name: 9K33M2 Osa-AK (9A33BM2): radars, radio, and NATO's view of them
status: First electromagnetic data set for the Osa-AK (October 2026). Performance anchors and geometry come from operator-country sources; internals that no public source gives (pulse width, PRF, noise figure, antenna gain) are labelled estimates derived from the published numbers. Calibration fits each radar's loop gain to its published detection range, so the estimates change ESM and jamming behaviour, not the published ranges. See docs/research/OSA_EM_SPEC_2026-10.md.
notes: Source ids are those of docs/SOURCES.md. Frequencies: operator sources say only 'centimetre band'; the values used are the centres of the bands Western sources report, for propagation only.

sources.title: V. Korovin, 'Зенитный ракетный комплекс «Оса» — история создания', Техника и вооружение 2010, part 2
sources.notes: Original 9A33B: search radar 250 kW pulse power, ~1e-13 W sensitivity, 1 deg azimuth beam, 4/4/19 deg elevation beams switched each turn at 33 rpm, fighter at 40 km (5 km altitude) / 27 km (50 m); tracking radar 200 kW, 2e-13 W, 1 deg beam, capture 23 km (5 km) / 14 km (50 m); both centimetre band; MTI; under strong jamming angles from the TV sight and range from the search radar.

sources.title: Przeciwlotniczy zestaw rakietowy 9K33M2 OSA-AK, MON Uzbr. 2112/80, Warszawa 1981 (JAWNE)
sources.notes: Printed page numbers. p10: MiG-21-type detection 20-35 km depending on altitude. p12-13: radio range at least 12 km with the radars on, 15 km off. p13-17: magnetron with AFC, TWT front end, TES (MTI) with internal or external coherence, double canceller; monopulse two-channel tracking radar resistant to repeater angle jamming; NLC low-target mode fixes the antenna elevation against ground reflection. p23: in TES only a 1.5 km segment around the tracked target is shown; NLC mode. p26: two R-123M radios. p66-67: siting rules, frequency plan, dummy-load checks.

sources.title: R. Wagner, flak11.de, 9K33 pages (NVA Fla-Raketen-Regiment 11)
sources.notes: Search radar coverage 45 km, 0-30 deg; beams I 0-4, II 4-8, III 8-28 deg; tracking radar 0-28 km, -12 to +78 deg, slew 15 deg/s.

sources.title: 9K33 Osa, English Wikipedia (citing Western references): Land Roll search radar H band (6-8 GHz), tracking radar J band (14.5 GHz)
sources.notes: Only used for the band centre (propagation, ESM band checks) and for NATO's threat-library view. Its 'frequency-agile' claim is not adopted: mon_2112_80 describes fixed working frequencies on a channel grid.

sources.title: US Army FM 100-2-3, The Soviet Army: Troops, Organization and Equipment, 6 June 1991 (distribution unlimited): SA-8 description p. 5-132
sources.notes: Used here only for the command link's band: 'two I-band guidance radars ... each one responding to a different frequency'. What the US Army believed, with 'probably'.

sources.title: R-123 'Magnolia': English Wikipedia; greenradio.de Eastern Mobiles R-123M page
sources.notes: 20-51.5 MHz in two sub-bands, 4 preset channels, 25 kHz spacing, ~20 W, 2.5 uV sensitivity.

radars.name: Osa-AK search radar (СОЦ; Polish RSWP)

prf_hz.notes: No public value. Chosen so the unambiguous range c/(2 PRF) = 75 km exceeds the 45 km coverage.

pulse_width_s.notes: 1e-13 W sensitivity with a ~10 dB noise figure implies ~2.5 MHz bandwidth, i.e. ~0.4 us pulses.

peak_power_w.notes: Original 9A33B; the AK's is not published.

gain_db.notes: G = 0.6 x 4 pi / (1 deg x 4 deg); 0.6 is a typical reflector efficiency.

beamwidth_el_deg.source: korovin_tiv_2010 (4 deg in the two lower positions)

centre_deg.source: korovin_tiv_2010 (27 deg in all); flak11 gives 8-28

emitter.notes: One beam per turn, switched each revolution (korovin_tiv_2010; mon_2112_80 p15). Working frequency chosen from a fixed grid per vehicle (mon_2112_80 p67): channel numbers are not public, so no channel list is given.

noise_figure_db.notes: TWT front end (mon_2112_80 p15); 10 dB with 2.5 MHz gives ~1e-13 W noise.

calibration.source: korovin_tiv_2010 ('истребитель на дальности 40 км при высоте полета 5 км')
calibration.notes: Original 9A33B. RCS 3 m2 and Pd 0.5 per scan are assumptions for 'fighter-type'. mon_2112_80 p10 gives 20-35 km for a MiG-21-type target on the Osa-AK, consistent with a higher Pd: the calibrated model gives Pd 0.8 near 30 km.

low_altitude_check.notes: Not fitted: reported by the calibration check against the propagation model.

antenna_height_m.source: estimate (antenna on the turret roof of the deployed vehicle)

range_resolution_m.source: derived from the 0.4 us pulse estimate

improvement_db.source: estimate; mon_2112_80 p15, p23 (TES, double inter-period subtraction)

mti.notes: Internal or external coherence (mon_2112_80 p15): external takes the phase reference from the chaff, cancelling wind-blown chaff (MtiMode::External).

tracker.notes: Processing choices for the operator's mental track on the PPI, not system data.

iff.source: mon_2112_80 p14, p16 (NRZ interrogator, antenna integrated with the search antenna); probability is an estimate

radars.source: korovin_tiv_2010; mon_2112_80; flak11; estimates as marked
radars.notes: Detection is calibrated to korovin's 40 km; the 27 km low-altitude figure is checked, not fitted (tests/test_em_data.cpp).

radars.name: Osa-AK tracking radar (ССЦ; Polish SSC)

prf_hz.notes: Unambiguous range 50 km > 28 km tracking range.

pulse_width_s.notes: 2e-13 W with ~10 dB noise figure implies ~5 MHz bandwidth.

peak_power_w.notes: Conflict: 180 kW (SAM Simulator), 18 kW (a flak11 page). Original 9A33B.

calibration.source: korovin_tiv_2010 (capture to automatic tracking at 23 km at 5 km altitude)
calibration.notes: The article prints '5000 км', an obvious misprint for 5000 m.

low_altitude_check.source: korovin_tiv_2010 ('14 км при высоте полета 50 м')

range_resolution_m.source: derived from the 0.2 us pulse estimate

improvement_db.source: estimate; korovin_tiv_2010 (SSC had MTI against chaff)

track_gate_m.source: mon_2112_80 p23 (TES shows a 1.5 km segment around the tracked target); samsim_osa p24

low_target_elevation_deg.source: flak11, samsim_osa p25 (НЛЦ lamp at 0-06...0-10 mils); mon_2112_80 p17 (NLC: antennas held at a set angle above the horizon against ground-reflection distortion)
low_target_elevation_deg.notes: 8 Soviet mils (6000 per turn), the middle of 0-06...0-10. Below it the tracking antenna stops following the target down.

eccm.source: angle_track_on_jam: samsim_thread (method 'Н': three-point guidance on the jammer's angles), korovin_tiv_2010 (angles from the TV sight, range from the search radar, under strong jamming); rgpo_susceptibility is an estimate
eccm.notes: mon_2112_80 p16-17: the two-channel monopulse resists repeater *angle* jamming; nothing public on range-gate pull-off.

radars.source: korovin_tiv_2010; mon_2112_80; flak11; estimates as marked

emitters.name: Osa-AK command transmitter, channel I (СПК)

freq_hz.source: estimate: frequency 3 of an eight-frequency grid spread over the I band fm100_2_3 gives
freq_hz.notes: mon_2112_80 p67: the command transmitter works on fixed frequencies, neighbouring vehicles interleaved (the 1st vehicle on 3 and 1, the 2nd on 4 and 2, the 3rd on 7 and 5, the 4th on 8 and 6); the frequencies themselves are not public.

prf_hz.notes: Pulsed command words; nothing public on the format.

gain_db.notes: A beam wide enough to hold the missile from the launch to the narrow beam.

emitters.notes: channels_hz: the vehicle's two grid frequencies (the 1st vehicle's 3 and 1, mon_2112_80 p67); СМЕНА ЛИТ. moves the channel to the other one (SAM3D's reading of the letter change). Switched on at ВНИМАНИЕ and radiating from then in combat; into its equivalent load only for peacetime checks (mon_2112_80 p67; scenario own_unit.em.command_link_in_load).
emitters.source: mon_2112_80 p67; fm100_2_3 (band); estimates as marked

emitters.name: Osa-AK command transmitter, channel II (СПК)

freq_hz.source: estimate: frequency 1 of the same grid
freq_hz.notes: mon_2112_80 p67 (the vehicle's second frequency); see channel I.

emitters.source: mon_2112_80 p67; fm100_2_3 (band); estimates as marked

emitters.name: 9M33 missile responder

freq_hz.source: estimate: in the tracking radar's band, whose antenna receives it

emitters.notes: The missile answers the station so its tracking antenna can follow it (the launcher's ЗАХВАТ, СР.Л, УЗКИЙ ЛУЧ lamps: captured in the wide, the medium, the narrow beam). Nothing public on its signal: every value is an estimate.

sensitivity_dbw.source: derived from r123_refs (2.5 uV into an assumed 75 ohm)

message_s.source: estimate (one designation read out: number, azimuth, range)

tracks_per_message.source: flak11 (designations to each vehicle by voice, azimuth and range)

range_anchor.source: mon_2112_80 p12-13 (radio range at least 12 km with the vehicle's radar transmitters working, at least 15 km with them off)
range_anchor.notes: System loss and co-site desense are fitted to these two ranges over flat open ground.

threat_libraries.name: NATO RWR view of the SA-8 (Western-reported bands)
threat_libraries.notes: What the blue side believed: band letters from Western sources. Wider than the truth on purpose; PRF and pulse width are unknown to us, so not constrained.
